dimensions.assessment: Affects artificial intelligence developers, industry stakeholders, research institutions, institutions of higher education, and federal agencies like NIST and CISA.
dimensions.evidence: The Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), in consultation with the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency... shall carry out a program

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a voluntary framework, definitions, and databases for tracking AI flaws without imposing mandatory compliance penalties on private entities.
dimensions.evidence: To direct the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop a program for the voluntary reporting of artificial intelligence flaws

dimensions.assessment: No specific appropriations or funding amounts are stated in the source text.
Requires new agency programs, multi-stakeholder convening, cooperative agreements, database establishment, and a congressional report within three years.
dimensions.evidence: develop, or enter into cooperative agreements with one or more eligible entity designated by the Director to develop, infrastructure for the voluntary reporting, collection, and tracking

dimensions.assessment: Permanent establishment of an ongoing national reporting program and database infrastructure.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than three years after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Director of NIST shall submit to Congress a report on the implementation of this section.

missing_information: Cost of establishing and maintaining the national database infrastructure.
importance_detail.rationale: Directs NIST to establish a voluntary program for reporting, collecting, and tracking artificial intelligence flaws, including developing taxonomies, technical standards, and reporting infrastructure.
